reason: planning stopped before any code was written: the critic judged that the reading misread the request: The reading contradicts itself: its expected deliverables list CHANGELOG.md (modify) and its defaults include the changelog default, but criterion 7 requires CHANGELOG.md to be untouched. Admission enforces the changelog default in code (admission.rs:819), so criterion 7's CHANGELOG clause cannot be met by an admitted candidate. (round 3 of 5). Verdict: revise. The core design is sound. It puts the guard where the pushes are made (GitRemote push/replace/delete_branch, and Git::push_branch/push_if_remote_at for every records-branch push) and builds the landing client from origin only. I checked the named files, line numbers, test doubles and seams in the snapshot: remote.rs, lib.rs:384/432, landing.rs:865-893, early.rs:363-462, ScriptRunner and UnreachedHost in gh/tests.rs, EarlyFake, early_seam::install, and hestia parse_spec, measure_problem and spec_gaps. Every existing production caller and test passes "origin". Every GitHub write in client.rs and pages.rs goes through `repos/{self.repository}`, so limiting the client's repository limits every PR, merge and rerun call. Two problems remain. (1) Blocker: the plan leaves CHANGELOG.md untouched. But the reading lists it as a deliverable and carries the changelog default, and `admission::changelog_required` (also called from producer.rs:446) sends the producer back and then refuses the candidate before the verifier. CHANGELOG.md is not marked read-only or excluded in athena.toml. So this plan cannot be admitted as written. (2) Major: `origin_url` relies on `git remote get-url --push origin` printing several lines when several push URLs exist. Without `--all`, git prints only the first URL, yet `git push origin` pushes to every push URL (or every `url` when no push URL is set). So a second push URL aimed at another repository passes the check. The planned multi-valued test would also fail against that code. Minor points: the landing-order claim rests on reading the code, and the guard checks the remote's name, not where it points; the spec text already states the second. Findings: minor: crates/athena-git/src/lib.rs is not among the reading's deliverables (files, crates/athena-git/src/lib.rs); blocker: Leaving CHANGELOG.md untouched gets the candidate refused at admission, before the verifier (Decision 7; step 9; criterion 7 demonstration; crates/athena-core/src/admission.rs:819-831, crates/athena-core/src/run/producer.rs:443-452 and 547-641); major: origin_url misses a second push URL, because `get-url --push` without `--all` prints only the first URL (Decision 4; step 2 (`origin_url`); criterion 4 demonstration case (b) 'a push URL set twice'); minor: No test shows that land_pr with no origin does no write; the claim rests on statement order (Decision 6; criterion 4 demonstration 'Landing order'; landing.rs:842-934); minor: The guard checks the remote's name, not its target; a GitRemote named origin is never checked against the push URL (Risks 2 and 4; step 9 mechanism text)
